subject.title: [Feature]: Support external unified session storage for stateless session mode

question: Should OpenClaw support external shared session storage as a core backend, a plugin/API seam, or defer it until the broader database-abstraction direction is settled?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but automation cannot choose dependency ownership, credential handling, config shape, migration semantics, transcript consistency, or core-versus-plugin support policy.

options.title: Design backend-neutral session storage
options.body: Define a storage contract for session metadata and transcripts first, then allow Redis/Postgres/Mongo-style implementations only after migration and consistency requirements are explicit.

options.title: Fold into database abstraction
options.body: Keep this issue open but block implementation on the broader backend-neutral database architecture in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/94675 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/90370.

options.title: Document external deployment only
options.body: Keep core local-store-first and document sticky sessions or external orchestration as the supported multi-instance deployment workaround for now.

recommendation.title: Design backend-neutral session storage
recommendation.body: Define a storage contract for session metadata and transcripts first, then allow Redis/Postgres/Mongo-style implementations only after migration and consistency requirements are explicit.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is product/architecture-wide and steipete has the strongest prior routing signal for adjacent scaling/session architecture issues.
